doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The violin teacher and weekly group lessons
summary: A fat white teacher wanted the fees; Haynes alone of the brothers took lessons at his mother's wish, though he wanted drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You mentioned the violin teacher. Could you describe him a little bit more? Do you remember his name?

No, I don’t remember his name, but he was a big fat white man. He had these coins in his pocket during the – when we’d be studying, he’d be shaking his – all I could hear is the money and all the kids playing out of tune. Got girls and boys. He says, “E, A, D.” He didn’t care if we hit the wrong notes. He just wanted those 50 cents, I imagine. So I do remember that about him.
He had them all in – everybody in the room?
Maybe 10 – between 10 and 15, something like that.
Were any of your other brothers taking lessons?
I have no idea. I guess I was very musical around the house, anyhow. But I wanted to play drums then.

Oh yes. My father, he was into me playing drums. I guess my mother just wanted me to do that for a while. I still may have that violin around there somewhere. Not the same house, of course, but – because my folks are all gone, but my brother has a house up there.
So it was your mother’s idea to take violin lessons?
It was my mother’s idea, yeah.
How long did you take lessons?
For quite a while. I don’t remember how long. At least over a whole season. Then I tried playing in school, in the band in school.
